results.title: How do tariffs work on imports? A shipper's guide to freight costs and supply chain planning
results.content:
| Cost component | Amount |
 --- |
| Product cost | $100,000 |
| International transportation | $6,000 |
| Insurance and customs fees | $2,000 |
| Domestic transportation | $4,000 |
| Total landed cost | $112,000 |

Now imagine a tariff adds $20,000 in additional import costs. The new landed cost becomes $132,000 before the product is sold or distributed. That increase affects margins, pricing decisions, internal processes and purchasing strategies throughout the supply chain. [...] A tariff announcement can change supply chain behavior almost overnight. When businesses expect import costs to rise, many accelerate orders, increase inventory purchases and move shipments earlier than planned. Warehouses fill faster. Transportation demand spikes. Capacity tightens in some lanes while other parts of the network slow down. [...] ### Inventory surges create freight volatility

One of the less visible effects of tariffs is the way they influence shipping behavior. When businesses anticipate higher duties, many accelerate imports to move inventory before new policies take effect.

This can create sudden increases in freight demand that affect:

 Port operations
 Warehouse capacity
 Equipment availability
 Transportation pricing
